newsitem.title: USA: Conn. business leaders like Rowland, hate taxes.
newsitem.headline: Conn. business leaders like Rowland, hate taxes.

text.p: Connecticut business leaders approve of the job Gov. John Rowland (R) is doing by a 62 to 18 percent margin, with 20 percent undecided, according to a Quinnipiac College poll released on Thursday.

Asked to rate the general business conditions in Connecticut, seven percent said "very good," while 28 percent said "good," 42 percent said "fair," 18 percent said "poor" and five percent "very poor," the poll found.
Some 29 percent expected conditions to improve in the next year, with 10 percent expecting them to worsen and 57 percent expecting no change.
According to 48 percent of those surveyed, taxes were considered the worst part of doing business in the state.
When choosing which tax they would like to cut, 37 percent said the personal income tax, while 15 percent said the gasoline tax.
"Business leaders want to see lower taxes," said Quinnipiac College School of Business Dean Phillip Frese.
"Specifically, they most want to see the personal income tax cut. A gas tax cut was the second most frequent answer given."
"A gas tax cut would help both individuals and business by bringing transportation costs down."
Rowland has called for cuts in both taxes.
"These results indicate that business leaders think his tax cut proposals are on the right track," Frese said.
Only 28 percent of the executives plan to increase their workforce, while three percent plan job cuts and 67 percent plan to hold their current job levels, the poll found.
The poll also found that by a 74 to 16 percent margin, business leaders said chief executives are over-compensated.
The poll was conducted April 21-30, with 400 executives at businesses throughout Connecticut.
